patch.title: Fed Holds Rates at 3.75%–4.00% in October 2026, With Two Dissents
patch.description: The Federal Reserve voted 10–2 on October 28, 2026 to hold its policy rate at 3.75%–4.00%. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: The official October 28 statement, released at 2:00 p.m. EDT, says “maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent”. This records the realized decision, not a forecast.
patch.longFormSummary:
• The October 28 decision left rates unchanged at 3.75%–4.00%; the vote was 10–2. Cook and Hammack favored a quarter-point increase.
  • The statement describes strong activity but persistent inflation; further evidence will guide policy. No future rate move is confirmed.
  • The hold followed September’s increase. Reuters reports policymakers waited for more inflation data.
  • Forecast comparison: the pin’s archived October 22 Kalshi snapshot favored a hold at 94%, versus 6% for a quarter-point hike; the realized hold matched that modal forecast. Its dollar-volume figure was a turnover proxy, not exchange-reported cash turnover.

patch.title: NAIA Opens on Las Olas on October 22, 2026
patch.description: NAIA opened on October 22, 2026 at 904 East Las Olas Boulevard in Fort Lauderdale, with coastal Mediterranean cooking and an Asian-influenced sushi program.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Resident states “Naia opens Thursday, October 22, 2026”; Axios independently reports the same Thursday. The operator now publishes dining hours, menus and reservations. This supersedes the earlier October18 target and November30 seasonal marker.
patch.longFormSummary:
• Resident gives October 22, 2026 as NAIA’s opening date, superseding the earlier tourism-board target of October 18.
  • The kitchen combines coastal Mediterranean dishes, live robata cooking and a separate sushi program.
  • Axios corroborates the October 22 opening.
  • The operator now accepts reservations and lists dinner hours and menus at the exact Las Olas branch.
